To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

capacity is a multidimensional construct and the most common dimensions are: the capacity of a resource to be utilized, the capacity of a process to deliver a service or product, the capacity of an organization to produce a service or product.

capacity is a complex construct that is difficult to define and measure; it is a multi-level construct, which is difficult to operationalize, but can be operationalized by focusing on the key elements of the construct; and the operationalization of the construct is dependent on the level of aggregation of capacity, the level of aggregation being determined by the purpose of the measurement.Originality/value – This paper contributes to the body of knowledge by developing a framework for the operationalization of capacity.
capacity is an actionable construct, which has been made visible by capacity metrics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural limits of capacity.
how capacity is perceived by the managers of a company.
the development of a capacity measurement framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the measurement dimensions identified are a necessary but not a sufficient condition for a capacity system.Originality/value – This paper is one of the first attempts to provide a detailed and comprehensive framework of capacity measurement dimensions.
capacity systems are not a panacea.
there are two types of capacity systems: one based on a single measure and the other on a combination of measures, each with its own strengths and weaknesses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new way of thinking about capacity.
the capacity of a firm is the maximum amount of work that can be accomplished in a given time, given the firm's available resources.
capacity is an important resource for organizations.

capacity is a visible and actionable construct.
there are two types of capacity metrics: one that is focused on measuring the capacity of the resources and another that is focused on the capacity of the organization.
capacity is a visible and actionable construct that can be measured and managed.
